Apple has acquired select assets from SigScalr, the developer behind the observability app SigLens, and has hired some of its employees. Here are the deal details.

Apple acquires part of SigScalr's business

Under the EU's Digital Markets Act, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, and Microsoft must notify the European Commission of acquisitions or other relevant transactions, after which the Commission publishes details of those deals on its website.

Today, the website was updated with a new acquisition by Apple involving SigScalr, a company that develops an observability platform called SigLens.

SigLens is an open-source observability platform designed to help developers collect, search, and analyse logs, metrics, and trace data generated by applications and infrastructure. SigScalr positioned it as a more efficient alternative to services like Splunk, Datadog, and Elasticsearch.

Speaking of the acquisition, here is a statement Apple submitted to the EU:

The completion date of the acquisition is listed as March 12th. Since then, SigScalr's official website has gone offline, and the main SigLens GitHub repository has been archived and placed in read-only mode.

In the archival notice, the developers wrote:

Today, we are officially archiving this project. First and foremost, we would like to express our heartfelt thanks to everyone for your support. 🙏 This project began as nothing more than a small idea, and thanks to your involvement, it grew into something far beyond what we ever anticipated. Your pull requests, bug reports, feature suggestions, stars, blog posts, tweets, and every word of encouragement made this project what it is today. Your trust in us, and the time you dedicated, means the world to us.

What do you think Apple will do with this acquisition? Let us know in the comments.
